title: Customer hands-on lab workshop: production POC agenda & facilitation notes
content:
Purpose:
Run a compact, hands-on lab during a 3.5 hour customer workshop to validate a Redwood-inference production POC path. This doc is a facilitator-first checklist + slide-by-slide outline and the exact scripts for the interactive exercises. Use it to ensure consistent customer experience across SEs and to minimize follow-up uncertainty.

Objectives (what success looks like):
- Customer can run a sample request end-to-end against a chosen deployment mode (hosted demo token or dedicated dev instance).
- Throughput/latency and cost estimates validated with a short synthetic workload.
- One concrete integration task (embedding search or chat tool call) executed and committed as a next-step ticket.
- Agreement on acceptance criteria, timeline (weeks), and rolloff plan.

Pre-work (sent 7 days before workshop):
- Request access: demo org invite and temporary API key (hosted) or VPN access and kubeconfig (dedicated/private).
- Short questionnaire: primary latency SLO, expected monthly tokens, data-sensitivity classification.
- Sample dataset: 500 docs (for embedding/search lab) uploaded to shared S3/GCS bucket.

Logistics and tech checklist (facilitator):
- Zoom + breakouts enabled, recording (opt-in).
- Dedicated Slack channel for workshop troubleshooting.
- Environment: demo org already pre-seeded with model variants + small routing policy. If not possible, prepare hosted API key.
- Laptop images: python 3.11 venv template, curl snippets, Node sample app.
- Bring: spare GPU instance (for side-by-side dedicated run), admin access to customer console if they want to try console rollouts.

Roles and timing (3.5 hours):
- Lead facilitator (SE): Maya Chen — agenda, slide walkthrough, demo 1, debrief.
- Runbook engineer: Diego Alvarez — environment orchestration, logs, toggle rollouts.
- Customer success partner: Priya Nair — contract/next-step capture, acceptance criteria alignment.
- Customer technical lead: (TBD) — joint troubleshooting and signing off acceptance test.

Agenda (high level):
- 00:00–00:10 Welcome & objectives (Lead)
- 00:10–00:25 Customer context & constraints (Customer TL: 5 min + Q/A)
- 00:25–00:45 Architecture & deployment options primer (Lead)
- 00:45–01:15 Live baseline test: hosted inference (Runbook)
- 01:15–01:30 Break
- 01:30–02:15 Hands-on lab A: embedding + approximate-nearest-neighbors integration (small team exercise)
- 02:15–02:45 Hands-on lab B: chatflow with function/tool calling and graceful fallback (paired exercise)
- 02:45–03:10 Performance tuning demo: batching, KV cache, quantization tradeoffs (Lead + Runbook)
- 03:10–03:25 Acceptance criteria & rollout plan (CS partner)
- 03:25–03:30 Wrap-up + next steps (Lead)

Slide outline and speaker notes (compact):
1) Title slide: "Hands-on POC Lab: [Customer] — Week of YYYY-MM-DD"
   - Note: state outcomes and key metrics we will validate.
2) Objectives & agenda
   - Note: call out explicit acceptance criteria up front.
3) Current architecture (customer-provided)
   - Note: quick sketch; annotate where inference will live. Ask one clarifying question.
4) Redwood deployment options matrix (hosted / dedicated / private)
   - Note: focus on tradeoffs relevant to the customer (SLA, cost predictability, data isolation).
5) Lab environment overview (end-to-end flow)
   - Note: show data path for embeddings/search and chat/tool-calls.
6) Baseline run: hosted inference demo steps
   - Speaker notes: run 10 sample requests, show latency/time-to-first-token, token counts, and trace link.
7) Hands-on lab A: embedding pipeline
   - Slide bullets: ingest -> embed -> ANN index -> query -> top-k rerank
   - Exercise script: provide curl + python snippets, sample dataset link, and expected outputs.
8) Hands-on lab B: chat + tool calling
   - Slide bullets: prompt design, function schema, fallback plan to smaller model
   - Exercise script: interactive prompt set and expected JSON outputs.
9) Performance tuning knobs
   - Bullets: batching window, KV cache warmup, quantization profile, autoscale rules
   - Mini-experiment plan: change batching and quantify latency vs cost over 200 requests.
10) Acceptance criteria & success metrics
   - Example metrics in slide: p95 latency <= 300ms (for short prompts), embedding recall @10 >= 0.78, monthly cost estimate <$X
11) Runbook & support model
   - Bullets: on-call, escalation, dedicated capacity contracts, SLO guarantees
12) Next steps / parking lot / action items

Facilitation scripts and prompts (copyable):
- Kickoff opener (Lead): "We're going to run two focused labs: an embeddings integration and a chatflow with tool-calling. By the end we want a clear go/no-go and a concrete ticket you own to move to pilot."
- Live demo narration (Runbook): "This request is routed to the hosted model. Observe the token breakdown in the console trace. We'll measure p95 across 10 repeated requests — note any variability."
- Troubleshooting prompt (for engineers): "If you see p95 > 800ms, open the trace and check if batching window is off or KV cache is cold. Toggle the caching policy and re-run."
- Breakout instruction: "Each breakout has 25 minutes: 15 minutes to complete the exercise, 10 minutes to collate outputs and pick one person to demo. We'll reconvene and discuss findings."

Hands-on exercises (detailed):
- Lab A: Embedding + ANN index
  - Input: sample-500.jsonl in shared bucket (link in linked_artifacts).
  - Steps: 1) run embedding script (python embed.py --api-key $KEY --input sample-500.jsonl) 2) index embeddings with FAISS via provided helper 3) run 10 queries and record recall@10 and median latency 4) commit one corrective prompt to improve recall if below threshold
  - Expected result: recall@10 >= 0.75 for provided dataset

- Lab B: Chat + function calling
  - Input: 20 prompt templates in prompts/chat-playbook.md
  - Steps: 1) POST chat request with function schema for 'search_papers' 2) verify correct function invocation JSON 3) deliberately trigger a fallback (simulate OOM) and confirm graceful degrade to smaller model with preserved context 4) capture conversation trace for audit
  - Expected result: function invocation correctness 100% on happy path, fallback retains last 3 messages context

Performance tuning mini-experiment (scripts):
- Baseline test: 200 single-shot requests at concurrency 8 -> record p50/p95/p99 and tokens per sec
- Toggle batching: switch batching window 5ms -> 25ms -> 100ms; rerun baseline and record latency/cost delta
- Toggle quantization profile: float16 vs int8 (if supported) -> record throughput and small-quality sample check

Acceptance criteria template (to capture during workshop):
- Functional: end-to-end call works with validated JSON traces (checkbox)
- Latency: p95 <= customer SLO or agreed fallback behavior (checkbox + measured value)
- Quality: embedding recall or chat quality threshold reached (checkbox + test ID)
- Ops: ability to rollout/rollback in console within 15 minutes (checkbox)
- Economics: projected unit cost per 1k tokens within 20% of the target (checkbox + estimate)

Common risks & mitigations:
- Risk: customer data is sensitive and can't leave VPC -> Mitigation: schedule Private deployment deep-dive and provide an on-prem quickstart image.
- Risk: cold cache p95 spikes -> Mitigation: pre-warm KV cache with sample traffic and set warmup policy.
- Risk: transient OOMs on large prompts -> Mitigation: model variant with reduced context or structured fallback to streamed responses.

Post-workshop outputs (deliverables we create within 3 business days):
- Short recording + 2-page summary with acceptance metric table (SE)
- Runbook draft with rollouts and rollback instructions (Runbook engineer)
- Follow-up ticket in Jira with owner, estimate, and acceptance criteria (CS partner)

Sample follow-up email (copy/paste):
"Thanks again for running the lab with us today. Attached is the 2-page summary with measured p95/p50 and recommended next steps. Our proposed next milestone is a 2-week pilot where we onboard 1k active users and validate latency under real traffic. Action item: please confirm which deployment you'd like to trial (hosted demo vs dedicated dev)."

Appendix: quick commands (for the lab)
- Embed: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '@sample.jsonl'
- Chat with function: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Find relevant policies"}], "functions":[{"name":"search_papers","parameters":{}}] }'
- Console trace link pattern: https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/{org}/traces/{trace_id}

Notes to facilitator (do not read aloud):
- Keep lab A small: if the customer's infra team wants to run the full embedding pipeline themselves, prioritize steps 1 and 2 and capture ownership for indexing.
- Watch for scope creep: if they ask for multi-language indexing, park it and estimate separately.
- Aim to leave with one committed ticket. A signed ticket is our best signal to start dedicated capacity discussions.

End of document.
